observations: I opened assets/panels/03-5.png, checkin-patients.png, main-cast.png and workflow/review/page-03.png with Read and looked at them myself.

Seating order from screen-left to screen-right is Mr. Raman, Priya, Ravi, as specified. This matches the order of the seated pair seen from behind in 03-3. All three look up toward the TV with small satisfied smiles.

Mr. Raman matches his sheet: white hair, bushy white brows, round glasses, prominent ears, cream half-sleeve shirt and grey trousers. His right hand (screen-left) holds the wooden stick upright beside his knee. His left hand rests on his knee. Both match production.

Priya matches her sheet: a high ponytail with a blue scrunchie (clearly visible), winged almond eyes, short straight brows, a beauty spot near her mouth, hoop earrings, the coral-pink block-print kurti, blue jeans and the slate crossbody bag. Her left hand (screen-right) holds the phone in her lap with the back facing out. Her right hand (screen-left) rests by the armrest and wears a thin bangle or watch. Both match production.

Ravi matches his sheet: beard, thick brows, light green shirt and dark trousers. His right hand (screen-left) holds his phone with the back facing out. His left hand (screen-right) rests on the dark-brown shoulder bag on his lap, and the wristwatch is on that wrist. Both match production.

The TV is in the upper right, at about the right third of the width and roughly the top third of the height. It shows a plain light-teal screen with one wide, empty white strip. No text or numbers are drawn. On page-03.png the lettered 'A-10 · A-11 · A-12' fits inside the strip. Neither phone screen is visible, so the panel shows no readable text or data.
Plain wall at the upper left takes the caption. On page-03.png the caption does not cover any face.

Minor continuity note, not blocking: the background waiting patients here (a man with glasses in a blue shirt, a woman with a bun in a mustard-yellow top) differ from the grey and brown patients in 03-1. The yellow-top figure is seen from behind and is small, so she is unlikely to be read as the vision-scene partner.
